cards.explanation: The answer is in the greatness of His strength. The text asks, "Who is this robed in splendor, marching in the greatness of His strength?" (Isaiah 63:1). Splendor on the outside, strength in every step, friends. I couldn't march like that if you gave me a tailwind and a gold base with wheels.
The answer is True. The One from Edom answers the question Himself: "It is I, proclaiming vindication, mighty to save." (Isaiah 63:1). He doesn't give a name here, friends. He tells you what He does.

The answer is someone who treads the winepress. The question asks, "Why are Your clothes red, and Your garments like one who treads the winepress?" (Isaiah 63:2). A winepress is where people trod on grapes to squeeze out the juice. Anybody who's done that comes out stained, friends, and I'd be the same way after a dive into the chocolate chips.
The answer is vengeance. The One from Edom says, "For the day of vengeance was in My heart…" (Isaiah 63:4). It's a heavy word, friends, and the text doesn't soften it. So we don't either.
The answer is False. The verse says, "…and the year of My redemption had come." (Isaiah 63:4). It's not far off at all, friends. It had come, and it sits right next to the day of vengeance.
The answer is False. There's no relief here, friends. He says, "I looked, but there was no one to help; I was appalled that no one assisted." (Isaiah 63:5). Appalled, plain and simple.

The answer is His own arm. The One from Edom says, "I looked, but there was no one to help…" and then, "So My arm brought Me salvation…" (Isaiah 63:5). No one helped Him, friends. His own arm did the work.
